title: NY State Assembly · District 79
area: The Bronx: Concourse Village, Melrose, Morrisania, Claremont, Belmont, and East Tremont

context.text: Both parties' primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled. Incumbent Chantel Jackson (D) advanced without appearing on the ballot. Emmanuel Findlay Jr. withdrew from the Republican primary but advanced from the Conservative Party primary without appearing on the ballot, so he appears on the Conservative Party line only.

candidates.name: Chantel Jackson
candidates.currentRole: Member, NY State Assembly, District 79 (since January 2021)

summary.text: Chantel Jackson is the incumbent Democratic Assembly Member for District 79 in the Bronx, seeking a fourth term. A licensed social worker, she chairs the New York State Legislative Women's Caucus and previously chaired the Black Legislative Task Force.

background.text: Jackson was born in Harlem; her mother immigrated from Belize and her late father was an entrepreneur and CEO of WIBO.
She earned a bachelor's degree in psychology from the City College of New York, then spent nine years working with low-income, first-generation students on college access and financial aid.

She earned a Master of Social Work from Adelphi University in 2014 and worked as a licensed social worker in New York City public high schools for four years, supporting students' mental and physical well-being.
She sits on the Assembly's Cities, Education, Housing, Mental Health, and Small Business committees, and chairs the Subcommittee on Micro Business.

priorities.text: Now in her third term at the time of the profile, Jackson focuses on maternal health, economic development, mental health, youth development, and holistic wellness.

As Chair of the New York State Black Legislative Task Force, she helped secure a $30 million investment for underserved communities and led a 12-stop statewide listening tour to ensure the funding reflected local needs.

In February 2026 she hosted The Next Wave Career Summit, bringing together professionals in content creation, photography, and entrepreneurship to equip students with tools and pathways into those fields.

Co-writing with state Sen. Cordell Cleare, Jackson said Albany budget proposals "restored funding to Aid and Incentives to Municipalities, increased tax revenue to New York City, restored funding for foster care, adult shelter costs, cash assistance for low-income families, and more — driving more than $5 billion more toward our city," arguing the state had shortchanged New York City and that Black families face the city's steepest affordability pressures.

record.text: Sponsored A7713, which changed adolescent-offender plea and Family Court removal procedures; it passed the Assembly and Senate and was signed into law (Chapter 809 of 2021).
As of the 2025-2026 session, serves on the Assembly's Cities, Education, Housing, Mental Health, and Small Business committees, and chairs the Subcommittee on Micro Business.

summary.text: Emmanuel Findlay Jr. is the Conservative Party candidate for Assembly District 79. He ran unsuccessfully for New York City Council District 16 in 2025 and for this Assembly seat in 2024, both times on the Republican and Conservative lines.

background.text: In the November 2025 general election for New York City Council District 16, Findlay received 11.4% of the vote (2,357 votes) running on the Republican and Conservative Party lines, losing to incumbent Althea Stevens.
In the November 2024 general election for this Assembly seat, Findlay received 3.3% of the vote (841 votes) on the Conservative Party line, behind Chantel Jackson (D) and Sharon Darby (R).

researchNotes: Jackson has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no source found gives a direct, on-the-record stance matching this guide's fixed issue list, so no Position entries are included for her despite her record; her priorities and record are otherwise documented in depth. Findlay has no campaign website, has not completed Ballotpedia's survey in any cycle, and has no record of prior officeholding, so his entry is marked 'minimal.'
